teams.heading: Andrew Durutalo named as the new Fiji men's high-performance head
teams.body: Former USA international Andrew Durutalo has been appointed as Fiji Rugby's new Head of Men's High Performance, tasked with strengthening the development pathways underpinning the national teams. Durutalo, who previously captained Fiji at age-grade levels before representing the United States, will oversee the transition of young talent into the senior set-up. The appointment comes as the national side searches for a new head coach ahead of their November test against France.

lead.why: Andrew Durutalo's appointment as Head of Men's High Performance represents a major structural shift for Fiji's rugby development and pathway system.

teams.heading: England winger Tommy Freeman commits future to Northampton with new contract
teams.body: Northampton Saints have secured the future of England winger Tommy Freeman, who signed a new contract to remain at Franklin's Gardens. The 25-year-old utility back, who has won 30 caps, follows international teammates Fin Smith, Fraser Dingwall and Alex Mitchell in recommitting to the Premiership champions. Freeman also featured in three Lions Tests against Australia last year. Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson welcomed the deal, calling the retention "a huge boost" for the club.

lead.why: Tommy Freeman has signed a new contract with Northampton Saints, committing his long-term future alongside several international teammates.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell issued blunt warning to Jimmy O'Brien before Ireland return
teams.body: Jimmy O’Brien has revealed the blunt motivation behind his unexpected Ireland recall during the July tour. The Leinster winger, who had spent years in the international wilderness, disclosed that head coach Andy Farrell delivered a characteristically direct ultimatum on the Sydney training ground, telling him: “You’re in, don’t f*** it up.” O’Brien took the advice to heart, starting all three Nations Championship fixtures against Australia, Japan and New Zealand. His redemption has catapulted him back up the pecking order.

teams.heading: Prop Rhys Carre wins Welsh Rugby Writers' Association player of the year
teams.body: Saracens loose-head Rhys Carre has been named the Welsh Rugby Writers' Association men's player of the season. The 28-year-old is the first prop to claim the honour since Gethin Jenkins in 2009. Having been dropped before the 2023 World Cup, Carre was recalled by boss Steve Tandy in 2025 and played 11 of Wales' 12 Tests last season. Carre said he was "honoured that the Welsh rugby media think I deserve it," while Cardiff centre Steffan Emanuel was named men's young player of the year.

lead.why: Prop Rhys Carre has been crowned the men's player of the season by the Welsh Rugby Writers' Association.

teams.heading: Argentina squad retains all-time peak of third in World Rugby rankings
teams.body: Argentina reached their highest ever position in the World Rugby rankings during the 2007-08 period. During that window, the national side climbed to No. 3 in the global standings. This remains the peak achievement for the team in the professional era. The side currently sits eighth in the Nations Championship log following three rounds of play. Following a 24-31 loss to England, the team has one win and two losses with 97 points for and 99 points against.

teams.heading: Les Kiss hands Jordan Petaia international recall for Springboks Perth Test
teams.body: Jordan Petaia returns to the Wallabies squad for the first time since the 2023 World Cup following a stint in the NFL. Head coach Les Kiss has also handed a surprise call-up to uncapped Western Force playmaker Harry McLaughlin-Phillips, who replaces the injured Carter Gordon after he suffered a leg fracture against Argentina. The squad, which includes a fit-again Zane Nonggorr, assembles in Perth on Friday. Kiss acknowledged the challenge of facing the back-to-back world champions, stating: "We still have a lot to work on."

lead.why: The return of Jordan Petaia from his NFL pursuit and the surprise call-up of a rookie playmaker are the day's dominant Wallabies storylines.

teams.heading: Mamoru Harada targets Pacific Nations Cup title ahead of Fiji final
teams.body: Japan are preparing for Saturday's Pacific Nations Cup final against Fiji following their 63-14 semi-final demolition of the United States. Hooker Mamoru Harada has confirmed the squad's target is to beat the Flying Fijians and win the championship, but Eddie Jones remains wary of lapses in discipline. Despite the nine-try victory in Osaka, Jones warned his side "lost a bit of concentration" during periods of the match. The Brave Blossoms now face a Fiji side seeking a fourth consecutive title after their semi-final win over Canada.

teams.heading: John Plumtree claims New Zealand may need bigger players to match South Africa
teams.body: Former assistant coach John Plumtree has warned that New Zealand may need to sacrifice mobility for size after being physically outmatched by South Africa. Despite an undefeated start to the Nations Championship, the fallout from the recent 3-1 series loss to the Springboks continues, with Plumtree telling the TMO podcast that the All Blacks looked "passive" in their own 22. He suggested that if the current personnel cannot stop gainline momentum or compete at the set-piece, Dave Rennie must consider selecting larger forwards.

lead.why: Plumtree's comments suggest a fundamental shift in selection philosophy following the physical defeat to South Africa.

teams.heading: Victor Matfield expects 'braver' Springboks as Rassie Erasmus prioritises experimentation
teams.body: Following the 3-1 series victory over the All Blacks, former lock Victor Matfield predicts a shift in approach as the team pivots toward upcoming challenges. Matfield notes that with the series pressure now lifted, the Springboks will likely become "a bit more brave with ball in hand" and experiment with more expansive attacking patterns. He also suggests that Rassie Erasmus will now look to rotate the squad, providing more opportunities for younger players to stake their claims for the 2027 World Cup.

lead.why: It outlines the future strategic direction of the team following the successful completion of the four-Test series.
